title: Vilasa 1. Lokanatha Gosvami
html:
Opening verses and glorifications; the life of Lokanatha: Talkhari, his going to the Lord in Navadvipa, his search for Mahaprabhu, the dream-vision and the prophecy of Narottama; Lokanatha in Vrindavana with the Gosvamis; in Ramakeli the Lord calls Narottama by name

1O you who are dear to those surrendered to the Lord of Sri, O king of dancers,
uniquely skilled in bestowing the treasure of your prema,
O friend of the life of Sri Gaura-Vishvambhara —
O Lokanatha, O Prabhu, be gracious to me!1

2I bow to Sri Lokanatha, the associate of Sri Chaitanya,
whose one life is Sri Radha-vinoda, who is the life of the people.

3I bow to Sri Narottama, dear to Sri Gaura,
a bee at the lotus feet of Lokanatha, maddened by the rasa of Radha and Krishna.

4I worship the branches of Sri Narottama Prabhu,
endowed with every good quality, removers of every anartha.

5For the delight of the Vaishnavas and to fulfil my own cherished desire,
I briefly relate the book called "Narottama-vilasa."2

6Glory, glory to Sri Gaura-Govinda, the Lord of all,
whose body, full of prema, enchants the worlds!

7Glory to the son of Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra,
glory, glory to the life of Nityananda and Advaita!

8Glory to the Lord of Gadadhara Pandita's life,
glory to the Lord of Srivasa, renowned in the world!

9Glory to Him who is subdued by the prema of Haridasa and Vakreshvara,
glory to Him who is expert in increasing Murari's joy!

10Glory to the friend of Gauridasa and Gadadhara,
glory to the Beloved of Narahari, full of majesty!

11Glory to the treasury of virtues, dear to Svarupa,
glory to the life of Sanatana, Rupa and Gopala!

12Glory, glory to the Lord together with the host of His devotees!
Reveal to me a little of the pastimes of Your devotees that I long for.

13O listeners, hear the words of a fool such as I;
seeing my destitution, be kind to me, all of you.

14I know neither good nor bad, I have no knowledge at all;
whatever I say, it is only the will of the sadhus that is strong in it.

15This book, the "Narottama-vilasa," is delightful:
correct it and relish it continually.

16In the order in which I made the mangalacharana in the preceding verses,
in that order I shall now speak — listen attentively.3

17Glory, glory to Lokanatha, dear to Sri Chaitanya,
the lamp of a brahmana family, renowned in every respect!

18Here I shall tell a little of his life —
listen: it is known throughout the world.

19In the land of Jessore there is a village named Talkhari:4
there he appeared, incomparable in every way.

20His mother was Sita, his father Padmanabha Chakravarti;
what can I say of how the two of them shone?5

21Padmanabha Chakravarti is known in the world:
Prabhu Advaita had great kindness for him.

22A great Vaishnava, extraordinary in all his deeds,
full of every virtue, the foremost of the brahmanas of Rarh.

23Day and night he was immeasurably intoxicated with sankirtana;
who could keep composure seeing the streams from his eyes?

24By the grace of Sri Advaita, with great joy in his heart,
he would constantly come to Nadia to see Gauranga.

25When he returned home, nothing pleased Padmanabha:
together with his wife he always sang of Gaurachandra's virtues.

26As was Padmanabha, so was his wife Sita —
a great Vaishnavi, devoted to her husband.

27Having obtained such a son as Lokanatha, the virtuous mother
raised him — how, I have no power to tell.

28Having dedicated her son to the feet of Gaurachandra,
she watched her son's doings with great joy.

29Sri Lokanatha had great eagerness on the path of bhakti;
beautiful in every limb, he was like compassion embodied.

30From a young age he was learned in all the shastras
and most diligent in serving his father and mother.

31He worshipped the feet of Krishna constantly
and by the power of bhakti drew all hearts to himself.

32When after some time his father and mother passed from sight,
he told his friends what was in his mind.

33Leaving worldly life and its pleasures like filth,
he set out for Nadia to see Prabhu.

34In Navadvipa he gave himself to Prabhu's feet,
and Prabhu graciously kept him near Himself.

35Prabhu, anxious at heart about the sannyasa He was to take,
quickly sent Lokanatha to Vraja.

36Who can understand Prabhu's doings? They are utterly deep:
having sent Lokanatha away, He Himself was not at ease.

37Lokanatha understood what was in Prabhu's heart:
in two or four days He would leave His home.

38Prabhu is the independent Lord, all is by His will:
what Lokanatha's journey was like, I cannot describe.

39Tears flowed incessantly from his eyes;
a day's journey took him four or five days.

40Some way along he heard that Prabhu had taken sannyasa
and, consoling His dear devotees, had gone to Nilachala.

41Remembering that the hair was no longer to be seen on Prabhu's head,
he wept aloud.

42Half dead, by Prabhu's order,
after some days he entered Vrindavana.

43He stayed some days, gazing at the beauty of Vrindavana,
and there he heard that Prabhu had gone to the south.

44Anxious at heart, Lokanatha
set off for the south, where Sri Gaurasundara was.

45Some way along he learned all the news:
Prabhu had returned from the south to Nilachala.

46Having set out for Vrindavana by the road through Gauda,
He had gone back to the Kshetra at the wish of the devotees.6

47Again Lokanatha heard that Prabhu had come to Vrindavana,
and at once he set out for Vraja.

48Coming to Vrindavana, he learned all the news:
in these very days Prabhu had left for Prayaga.

49Grieved, Lokanatha resolved firmly:
"At dawn I shall go to Prayaga to see Prabhu."

50Remembering Prabhu's virtues, he wept;
he rolled on the ground, and none could hold him.

51At the end of the night, by Prabhu's will, he fell asleep
and in a dream saw Gaurachandra in Nadia:

52His body anointed with sandal, like pure gold,
flowers arranged in His lovely curling hair,

53a divine tilaka on His forehead, the sacred thread on His neck —
who would not be enchanted by the play of His eyes and brows?

54How sweetly He smiles and smiles with His gentle mouth,
destroying the pride of the moon and showering nectar!

55What arms reaching to the knees, what a broad chest!
He wore a lovely cloth tucked in three places.

56Every limb was adorned with jewelled ornaments;
His age was youthful, and in it waves of rasa.

57With sweet words He said to Lokanatha:
"I always abide here together with all of you.

58Here in Navadvipa My pastimes are endless;
not even Brahma and the others can reach their limit."

59Having said this and more, He began to embrace Lokanatha —
and he awoke, unable to bear his grief.

60By Prabhu's will sleep drew him in again,
and again Prabhu appeared before Lokanatha —

61Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the crown of sannyasis —
and spoke to Lokanatha in the sweetest words:

62"You have resolved to go to Prayaga —
why should you go? See, here I am before you.

63O Lokanatha! I had a great longing at heart
to live together with you in Vrindavana.

64That is why I quickly sent you to Vrindavana
and Myself took sannyasa from Bharati.

65I was eager to see the forest of Vrinda,
but that did not come to pass; I went to Advaita's house.

66All were in great sorrow at My sannyasa;
staying at Advaita's home, I consoled them all.

67Knowing everyone's wish, I went to Nilachala;
having stayed there some days, I travelled through the south.

68For My sake you too set out for the south;
I came to Vraja, and hearing of it you came to Vraja.

69As fate would have it, we did not meet;
there is no reckoning the sorrow you suffered.

70Hearing from people that I had gone to Prayaga,
you resolved to go there at dawn.

71I am always near you —
do not go anywhere away from Vrindavana.

72From Prayaga I shall go to Nilachala,
and you will hear all that befalls Me.

73Sanatana, Rupa and others dear to Me
you will very soon see here.

74Through them I shall reveal the wish of My heart,
and an ocean of happiness will surge up in Vrindavana.

75On the waves of that happiness you will float always,
and all that is in your heart will be fulfilled.

76After some time a king's son
will become your disciple; his name will be Narottama.

77He will always float in the rasa of prema-bhakti
and will easily destroy the impurity of living beings.

78He will reveal a lofty and most sweet singing,
on hearing which even wood and stone will melt."

79Having said this, He embraced Lokanatha,
and Lokanatha, falling to the ground, bowed at His feet.

80At that moment sleep broke and Prabhu vanished;
in his distress Lokanatha could hardly keep his life.

81Remembering and remembering the virtues of Gaurangachand,
he sighed and wept with stifled sobs.

82After a while he consoled himself and grew calm,
yet still streams of prema flowed from his eyes.

83Seeing that morning had come, he performed his morning duties
and, sitting in solitude, chanted the holy name.

84At the request of the brahmanas of Vraja, at the proper time
he ate fruits and the like, and lived beneath a tree.

85He never stayed long in one place,
but wandered about the region of Vrindavana.

86Seeing a wondrous beauty of the forest somewhere,
he would remain there some days in secret.

87Suddenly he heard from someone
that Sri Subuddhi Mishra had come to Vrindavana.7

88Then Sri Rupa Gosvami came
and went back again to where Sri Gaurasundara was.

89Sanatana came and went on to Nilachala.
Hearing all this, Lokanatha shed tears of prema.

90Crying "Sanatana! Rupa!" he would sigh:
"When shall we live together?"

91As he spoke thus, in utmost agitation,
a voice came from the sky: "They will come soon."

92How Rupa and Sanatana came after some days —
all that is described at length in other books.

93Sri Gopala Bhatta and others came to Vrindavana,
and Lokanatha Gosvami met with all of them.

94What joy there was at their meeting —
I, a fool, cannot describe even a trace of it.

95Sri Rupa Gosvami always pleased
Lokanatha Gosvami with respect in every way.

96What Sanatana Gosvami's attitude to him was,
he himself made known in his book.

97Thus in the Vaishnava-toshani:
I bow to those dear to Vrindavana, who have taken shelter at the feet of Sri Govinda —
to Sri Kashishvara, Lokanatha and Sri Krishnadasa.8

98With Sri Gopala Bhatta, Raghunatha Bhatta and others,
Lokanatha was ever overwhelmed with prema.

99Together with them Lokanatha, absorbed in prema,
enjoyed pastimes in Vrindavana with gladness of heart.

100I cannot describe his wondrous life;
well known is his friendship with Bhugarbha Gosvami:

101their body and mind were one, in nothing different —
most wonderful was the love between the two.

102I cannot expand here on their love;
Lokanatha was in every way after his heart.

103What shall I say? Hearing of the Gosvami's renunciation,
even a heart hard as stone splits apart.

104Ever independent of all, in full accord with the scriptures of bhakti,
he was devoted to the service of the Deity Sri Radha-vinoda.

105How he obtained Sri Radha-vinoda
is made known in the Bhakti-ratnakara.9

106As he gazed on the sweet beauty of Sri Radha-vinoda,
he suddenly beheld the sweet beauty of Gaura.

107Then he remembered Prabhu's command in the dream,
and, overwhelmed with prema, could not stop his tears.

108Speaking of the lovely deeds of Gaurangachand,
he would swoon and roll on the ground.

109He constantly reproached himself
for not having seen the wonderful pastimes of Gauranga.

110When Krishnadasa Kaviraja asked the Gosvami
for permission to write his book,

111the Gosvami gladly gave him permission,
but forbade him to describe himself in it.

112When he went for permission to Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosvami,
he too, with great regret, forbade him in the same way.10

113These accounts I heard from the lips of the elders;
I have described a little — fortunate are those who relish it.

114Lokanatha Gosvami is supremely merciful,
a vessel of Sri Chaitanya's mercy, full of the jewel of prema.

115He lived ever in Vrindavana; who can fathom his intent?
With a pleased heart he bestowed his mercy on Narottama.

116Thus in these verses:11
He whose only wealth is the mercy of Krishna-Chaitanya, whose heart is rich with the golden ornaments of prema for Him —
falling to the ground we bow to him constantly; we take shelter of him, Lokanatha Prabhu.

117He who obtained eternal residence in Vrindavana, in whom Krishna's pastimes and rasa shine forth, who follows his own good conduct ceaselessly and without rest — we take shelter of him, Lokanatha Prabhu.

118Whose power of mercy the great sage named Narottama came to know,
whose detachment from worldly things is vast — we take shelter of him, Lokanatha Prabhu.

119Glory to Sri Thakura Mahashaya Narottama,
the dearest disciple of Lokanatha Gosvami!

120Krishnananda Datta, the elder brother of Sri Purushottama —
his son is Narottama, known everywhere.

121How Narottama was born in his house
I cannot describe here at length,

122yet I shall tell something of it — listen carefully:
it is the greatest joy to hear.

123In Gauda there is the village of Ramakeli, a wonderful settlement;12
there lived Rupa and Sanatana Gosvami —

124ministers of the great king, expert in all the shastras,
always engaged in discussing the shastras with scholars.

125Maharashtra, Karnataka, Dravida, Tailanga,
Utkala, Mithila, Gauda, Gujarat, Vanga,

126Kashi, Kashmir and other lands — great scholars from there
were honoured in their assembly.

127Their wondrous fame spread through the world —
I have told something of it at length in the Bhakti-ratnakara.

128Sanatana and Rupa were very dear to the king of Gauda;
their opulence was boundless and all their ways were wonderful.

129Hearing from people that in Navadvipa
Sri Gaurasundara was performing His pastimes, they rejoiced at heart

130and again and again sent Prabhu humble letters —
this is set forth in the book Chaitanya-charitamrita.

131Having surrendered themselves at Prabhu's feet, intent,
they always longed to see Prabhu.

132Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the Lord of all, subject to His devotees,
was anxious at heart for Sanatana and Rupa.

133Having taken sannyasa and gone to Nilachala,
Prabhu, consoling His dear devotees, set out for Vrindavana.

134Prabhu's way lay through the land of Gauda;
His dear devotees would not leave His company.

135Hundreds of thousands of people ran to see Prabhu;
thus Prabhu Gaura Raya came to Ramakeli.

136Here Sanatana and Rupa, at Prabhu's coming,
floated with their circle in an ocean of great happiness.

137Keshava Chhatri and all the others dear to them13
were filled with great jubilation.

138The royal ministers Sanatana and Rupa, in secret,
first met Prabhu together with His dear associates.

139Prabhu Nityananda showed great mercy:
it was he who brought the two of them to Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra.

140Meeting them, Sri Gaurasundara with a joyful heart
sprinkled them with nectar in many sweet words.

141Prabhu Nityananda, Haridasa, Vakreshvara,
Mukunda and all the rest were immensely happy.

142In what joy Sanatana and Rupa were immersed
by Prabhu's mercy — who can describe it?

143Mahaprabhu stayed there only a few days,
and there was no end to the crowds of people.

144Seeing Prabhu, people could not be still;
they swam continually in the ocean of the bliss of prema.

145Who can understand Prabhu's wondrous pastimes?
What to speak of others — even yavanas floated in prema!

146One day Prabhu, with His dear associates,
danced in sankirtana, intoxicated with great prema.

147Gazing in the direction of the village of Sri Kheturi,
He shed wondrous streams of bliss from His eyes

148and called out again and again, "Narottama!" —
out of love for His devotee He could not be still.

149The ocean of mercy, Prabhu Nityananda Raya,
roared aloud with great joy in his heart.

150Haridasa, Vakreshvara and the others, full of prema —
great gladness rose in their hearts.

151Seeing Prabhu's wondrous state, everyone
whispered to one another:

152"Prabhu says the name 'Narottama' again and again —
from this we have understood something of the reason:

153there is a vessel of Prabhu's prema named Narottama,
and he will appear in some village of this land.

154We do not know which fortunate man
will obtain such a son, full of love for Prabhu.

155She who bears such a Narottama in her womb —
there is none in the world as fortunate as she.

156Through Narottama much will be accomplished."
Something of this became evident in Prabhu's ecstatic absorption.

157In the same way, in Nilachala, Prabhu, the enchanter of the worlds,
wept, repeating the name "Srinivasa."

158In whose house Srinivasa would appear,
that Mahaprabhu revealed to the world.

159His father Sri Chaitanya Dasa and his mother Lakshmipriya
both went to Nilachala and saw Prabhu,

160and then by Prabhu's order the two returned to Gauda;
and I with great joy saw them both there.14

161The Lord's devotees said to one another:
"Through Srinivasa much will be accomplished.

162Gaurahari will manifest an embodiment of prema —
shall we see such a Srinivasa to our eyes' content?"

163Thus they spoke of many things — I heard it with my own ears.
Who can understand Prabhu's pastimes?

164In Nilachala Prabhu made Srinivasa known,
and coming to Ramakeli He drew Narottama to Himself.

165"Srinivasa and Narottama are Prabhu's servants:
will the two of them come before our eyes?"

166Saying many such things with great joy at heart,
they gazed on Gaurangasundara amid the assembly of devotees.

167Thus Prabhu, overwhelmed in ecstatic absorption,
danced and wept, calling the names of devotees to come.

168O brothers, how wonderful are the deeds of Chaitanya!
He made the village of Ramakeli supremely holy.

169Bound by the love of Sanatana and Rupa,
He saw Kanai-natashala and went back to Nilachala.15

170These accounts spread everywhere,
and all longed for Narottama to appear.

171Listen to all this continually and with care:
Narahari tells the Narottama-vilasa.

Thus ends the first vilasa of the Narottama-vilasa.

Notes

  1. The verse admits a double reading: the name "Lokanatha" means "lord of the worlds," and the whole address can be taken as referring to Gaura Himself (the Consort of Sri, king of dancers in sankirtana, bestower of His own prema). In its direct sense it addresses Lokanatha Gosvami, Narottama's guru.
  2. The "branches" (shakha) are Narottama's disciples and followers; Vilasa 12 is devoted to them.
  3. The author follows the order of the opening verses: first Lokanatha (Vilasa 1), then Narottama, then his "branches."
  4. The text has Talgari (তালগড়ি); usually Talkhari, north of Jessore (now Bangladesh).
  5. "Shone" follows the 1924 edition (কান্তি); the 2021 edition has "fame" (কীর্তি).
  6. Following the 1924 edition ("গৌড়পথে," "by the road through Gauda"); the 2021 edition has "Lokanatha" here. This refers to Mahaprabhu's first attempt to go to Vrindavana through Gauda, when He turned back to Puri from Ramakeli (Kanai-natashala) (CC Madhya 1; below, vv. 133–169).
  7. Subuddhi Raya (Mishra), a former ruler of Gauda who became a Vaishnava and settled in Mathura (CC Madhya 25).
  8. A verse from the opening of the Vaishnava-toshani, Sanatana Gosvami's commentary on the tenth canto of the Bhagavata.
  9. BR 2: Radha-vinoda Himself came to Lokanatha (according to tradition, from the forest near the village of Umrao) and gave Himself to him.
  10. Cf. the CC: Krishnadasa Kaviraja writes almost nothing about Lokanatha and Gopala Bhatta — at their own request.
  11. The 1924 edition names no source; the 2021 edition ascribes these verses to Vishvanatha Chakravarti's Stavamrita-lahari (his octet on Lokanatha).
  12. Ramakeli is a village near Gauda (close to present-day Malda), where Rupa and Sanatana, ministers of Sultan Husain Shah, lived (CC Madhya 1).
  13. Keshava Chhatri, a dignitary at the court of Gauda (CC Madhya 1).
  14. "I saw" — so in both editions (মুই … দেখিলু); since the author lived in the eighteenth century, these are presumably the words of an eyewitness whose account he passes on (cf. v. 163: "I heard it with my own ears").
  15. Kanai-natashala, a place near Rajmahal, from where the Lord turned back to Puri (CC Madhya 1).
